section_summary: The concluding page of a report says Japan’s stabilization program nearly curbed inflation, while falling exports and investment reduced demand and held back production. It argues that substantial investment is needed for reconstruction, modernization, and a growing population, alongside continued stabilization and industrial rationalization.

people.name: Johnston
people.role: Named in the title of the Johnston Report; no role stated

subfiles.title: Conclusion
subfiles.about: The report assesses the effects of economic stabilization and the investment needed for Japan’s recovery.
subfiles.summary: Stabilization nearly curbed inflation, but weak demand stalled production. The report calls for investment and continued rationalization.
